title: Rebuild and re-exec Athena after drain lands changes to its own code
summary: After drain lands a change touching crates/, xtask/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock or setup.sh, it runs the setup.sh build/install steps, then re-execs with the remaining budget and job limit; a failed rebuild stops with 'rebuild failed' plus build output. status and agent-running commands (go, drain, audit, audience) print one stale-build line when the installed build commit is older than HEAD for those paths. Audience: the operator running drain unattended.

defaults_applied.how: New tests for rebuild, failure and status line; fmt, clippy -D warnings and cargo test pass.
Tests check that the rebuild ran once and the second item ran under the new build commit, not only that wiring exists.
Criteria check the drain continuing unattended across a landing.
Verifier runs cargo test, clippy and fmt --check.
One focused change in the named files.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The build commit is already embedded in the binary (or is added at build time by the same steps as setup.sh); the producer finds how setup.sh records it.
Rebuild and install are behind an injectable step so tests use a fake instead of running cargo.
Re-exec carries remaining budget and job limit as arguments to the same drain command.
The stale check compares the build commit with HEAD using git diff limited to crates/, xtask/, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, setup.sh.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run cargo test: a test drains two fake items where the first landing changes a crates/ file; it shows the rebuild step ran exactly once and the second item ran under the new build commit.
Run cargo test: a test shows a failed rebuild stops the drain with stop reason 'rebuild failed' and includes the build output.
Run cargo test: a test shows status prints the stale-build line when a crates/ file changed after the build commit, and prints none when only docs/ or records/ changed.
go, drain, audit and audience print the same one-line stale-build warning when the build commit is older than HEAD for the watched paths.
The re-exec passes the remaining budget and job limit.
cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy with -D warnings and cargo test all pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry describing the self-rebuild and stale-build warning.

out_of_scope: Rebuilding after landings that touch only docs/ or records/
Changing config schema or the planner model settings
departures: Higher cost and lower pass probability than reference: touches drain control flow, re-exec and git-based staleness, and needs several tests.
urgent_reason: Removes manual ./setup.sh reruns and failed landings caused by a stale binary, cutting rejected attempts and stalls.
hard_reason: It changes landing flow in drain (rebuild and re-exec after landing) and stop handling, where mistakes are costly and hard to see.
